name: Holy Trinity Church, Murree
assumptions: No footprint exists in OSM; the plan is sized from the Esri image and the photos: nave about 11.5 by 24 m, whole building about 38 m long.
Heading 154 and origin come from the red and grey roof seen on a z18 Esri tile; trees hide part of the roof, so position may be off by several metres.
Tower is placed at the south-south-east end by matching the repainted red slope to the side where Dawn 2018 shows the tower on the right.
Heights are estimated from door and window proportions, assuming a 2.7 m door: eave 7.2 m, ridge 12.9 m, tower top about 25.6 m.
Bays are about 3.4 m, seven a side; the count comes from the Wikipedia photo and may be off by one.
Chancel block size, 13.6 m wide, 7.5 m deep, eave 5 m, ridge 8.6 m, is read from one oblique photo.
How the door gable, the rear small gable and the timber porch wing sit relative to each other could not be fully reconciled between photos; Dawn 2018 is followed.
The west side has red sheet and the east side rust sheet, as photographed in different years; the true current colour of the east slope is unknown.
Wall colour is the tan of the 2018 and 2020 photos; sources call it grey brick.
South face of the tower and the south face of the nave are unseen; a plain door is assumed on the tower south face and the same belfry windows on every side.
Window fill is a diamond lattice texture; stained glass patterns are not modelled and no night lighting is added because none is documented.
Bishop's house, library, graves and compound walls are left out because no photo places them.
